To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) HCV Core antigen is a good predictor of SVR during triple therapy, (2) HCV Core Ag is more predictive of SVR than HCV RNA at week 4 of triple therapy, (3) HCV Core Antigen should be used in conjunction with HCV RNA in the monitoring of triple therapy.

HCV core antigen (Ag) testing is a useful adjunct to monitoring the virological response of chronic HCV patients treated with the protease inhibitor (PI) triple therapies, telavivir (TVR), and boceprevair (BOC) with pegylated interferon alfa and ribavirin.
HCV antigen measurement may be a useful alternative to viral RNA monitoring in the management of HCV infection treated with direct-acting antivirals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of hepatitis C core antigen testing in monitoring virologic response to HCV protease inhibitor-based triple therapy.
the development of new diagnostic tools for HCV infection, with the aim of developing new tests for monitoring HCV infection and treatment.
the role of HCV antigen as a potential surrogate marker of virological response during PI-based triple therapy in the era of DAAs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the role of antigen measurement in the monitoring of DAA therapy is yet to be defined.
in the era of DAA therapies, the role of HCV core antigen is limited to a few selected patients, but it is not a replacement for viral RNA monitoring.
the HCV antigen assay is not a useful marker of treatment response in the era of DAAs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the HCV antigen is an important predictor of SVR in patients undergoing PI triple therapy.
HCV core antigen testing is a potential alternative to viral RNA monitoring for assessing treatment response in patients treated with PI triple therapy.
HCV core antigen is a good surrogate marker for viral RNA in the early stages of DAA therapy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HCV core antigen is a good surrogate marker to monitor viral kinetics in the era of DAA-based regiments.
HCV core antigen is a potential marker of early response in HCV patients undergoing DAA therapy, and that this marker should be further investigated in the context of DAA-based regiments.
the HCV core antigen is an early predictor of response to PI therapy and can be considered as a useful tool for monitoring treatment response.
